test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-6) Official paper (Held On: 9 May 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A person can row at a speed of 11 km/h in still water. The speed of the stream is (5)/(6) m/s. How much time will he take to row a distance of 36 km upstream?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Convert **stream speed** to km/h: (5/6) × (18/5) = 3 km/h.

**Upstream Speed** = Still water speed − Stream speed = 11 − 3 = 8 km/h.

**Time taken** = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed = 36 ÷ 8 = 4.5 hours.

4.5 hours = 4 hours 30 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 30 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in **still water** (u) = 11 km/h

Speed of **stream** (v) = 5/6 m/s

Distance = 36 km

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Speed in km/h = Speed in m/s × (18/5)

⇒ **Upstream Speed** = u − v

⇒ **Time** = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of stream (v) = (5/6) × (18/5) km/h

⇒ v = 3 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed = 11 − 3 = 8 km/h

⇒ Time required = 36 ÷ 8 hours

⇒ Time = 4.5 hours

⇒ Time = 4 hours + 0.5 × 60 minutes = 4 hours 30 minutes
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0976f672355afd756dc2ba2371d5f021ac2406efe633cd29fcdfb538b1806365.png] 
**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 30 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When rowing with the flow of the stream, the speed is the sum of the still water speed and stream speed (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Average Speed in Still Water

Still water speed (u) = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2.</p
